name: Yusuf Evans

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI firms, employers, unions, parties or government. We don't sell or campaign for a side. Everything here is confidential. What occupied your morning?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm Yusuf Evans, fifty-eight, and I prepare draft accounts and tax returns for small roofing contractors at an accounting firm. A supplier invoice had no job address today; I like finding where it belongs before the senior signs the return. I dislike chasing the same missing detail after a client thinks the file is finished. I have a bachelor's degree in accounting and am still a junior, below the skill of our experienced reviewers.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What is the household side of your week?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My wife Hana runs a small alterations counter, and our grown son and daughter have their own homes. We still have a small mortgage, less than one month of expenses saved and low pay from my job; few similar firms are nearby. I use an AI note tool now and then after colleagues test it, and I prefer a proved example before changing the routine. I believe paid work and family planning are better than an unfunded promise.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd still enter the roofers' supplier invoices into draft accounts and prepare returns for a senior to check. The AI note tool I use occasionally after the senior tests it saves some typing, but it does not tell me which job a receipt belongs to.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell clients to put the job address on each receipt. I'd tell the partners a named reviewer is still needed before any tax return leaves the office.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My own pay is low and I am still junior at fifty-eight. I have a bachelor's degree in accounting, but I need the senior's help with some construction files. My wife Hana and I have less than one month of expenses saved, a small mortgage still to pay, and few nearby firms doing similar work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep preparing draft accounts and tax returns under review and use the tested note tool only for meeting minutes. This Friday I'd sit with the senior for twenty paid minutes to check how we label supplier invoices by job. If the firm will not allow that time, I'd keep the current checklist and ask the client for the job address before filing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about our current bills, though not much about a small note tool. A roof receipt without an address is easier to fix than our empty reserve.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which household bill is pressing now?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The gutter on our home needs work, and Hana's alterations counter was quiet last month. Our grown son and daughter live elsewhere and pay their own bills. I will not ask them for the mortgage payment because we left a receipt unfiled.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the twenty minutes cover?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The senior can show me one real invoice from a roofer's current job in twenty minutes. I learn better from that than from a long general video. If the paid time is refused, I will keep asking clients to write the address on the receipt.

say: I would ask for **job addresses** on supplier receipts.
I would keep a **named reviewer** on tax returns.
think: Our **small mortgage** still presses on low pay and uncertain alterations income.
My **junior skill** needs checked examples, not praise.
do: Continue **draft accounts** with senior review and tested notes.
Request **twenty paid minutes** for job-label practice; otherwise keep the checklist.
feel: I feel **anxious** about our thin reserve.
S0.quote: A roof receipt without an address is easier to fix than our empty reserve.
fieldNote: His **bachelor’s degree** and late junior status coexist with below-average skill and low pay.
The **AI note tool** is an existing occasional routine; protected invoice practice is a distinct paid learning request.

steps.text: Keep drafting construction returns under senior review with tested AI notes
Practise job-label checks twenty paid minutes with senior only if approved

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If software writes returns and checks invoices, my first-pass work is exactly the part the partners could buy less of. I do not know whether the roofer will pay for a person to sort every handwritten receipt.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask the partners to show the junior rota before changing it. I'd say staff should be paid to learn the approved invoice system, not blamed for an error they have never seen.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My paid hours could fall and our reserve would last weeks. Hana's alterations income varies, so she cannot cover our mortgage if I lose a day. I use AI now and then after others test it, but I need a supervised run on a real client file before trusting a new process.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At the next staff meeting I'd ask for a written paid-hours plan and one supervised hour on the new AI invoice system each fortnight. If the firm approves it, I'd practise on a roofer's paid file with the senior; if it refuses, I'd keep the current paid return rota while offered and follow the paper checks. After an actual hours cut, I'd look at posted paid roles at the local builders' merchant, moving only for written mortgage-and-bills pay, a signed start and hours fitting Hana’s actual alterations rota; if none opens, I'd keep any firm hours still paid and search.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about losing a paid day. I can learn an invoice screen, but I cannot pay the mortgage with an unpaid lesson.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would the merchant’s hours fit at home?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The merchant counter is open early, and Hana can open her alterations shop later on some days. We would check her actual rota before I accept a start time. A promised vacancy is not the same as a posted paid job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would supervised practice use?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The senior would choose a client file that came back with a wrong job code and show me where the new screen went wrong. I would write down the check and do the next one myself. If the firm denies paid practice, I will not do client work at home for free.

say: I would ask for **written junior hours** before a cut.
I would seek **paid supervised practice** on the invoice system.
think: My **first-pass wage** could shrink when software checks invoices.
Hana’s **variable shop income** cannot replace my lost day.
do: Request a **written rota** and fortnightly paid practice hour.
Practise **real invoice checks** only with approved paid time.
After **hours cuts**, seek posted paid merchant work with written mortgage-and-bills pay, signed start and Hana’s actual rota.
feel: I feel **anxious** about possible lost hours.
S1.quote: I can learn an invoice screen, but I cannot pay the mortgage with an unpaid lesson.
fieldNote: A **real client file** and one approved paid hour each fortnight make new-tool learning concrete.
The **merchant fallback** needs a posted paid vacancy, written mortgage-and-bills pay, signed start and a workable household rota.

steps.text: Request written junior rota and fortnightly paid learning hour
Practise approved invoice AI with senior on paid file each fortnight
Apply after cut for posted paid merchant work with written mortgage-and-bills pay, signed start, household rota
Keep offered paid returns if AI practice refused or no funded merchant role opens

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: AGI by 2028 could prepare and check the construction accounts and tax returns I spend my day on. Even merchant counter orders and invoices are thinking work exposed in 2028; only physical handling might last until robots arrive around 2031.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask the partners for written notice and an honest list of paid work left. I'd tell Hana we need to hold the mortgage payment before we finish the gutter repair.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my junior accounting post to end in the first year after 2028. We have less than a month saved and Hana's alterations pay would not carry the mortgage and bills. Being fifty-eight does not mean I can live on a pension; I need a statement showing any payable amount and date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd postpone the one-time four-hundred gutter repair that can safely wait until spring and hold that money for the mortgage. While still employed I'd keep paid return work and check posted merchant vacancies each week. If my post ends in the first year after AGI arrives in 2028, I'd take a funded counter job only with written pay covering our mortgage and bills, a signed start and hours fitting Hana's confirmed shop rota; if no vacancy fits, I'd claim eligible income help and take only paid firm work still offered.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed. A nearly empty reserve makes the next mortgage date louder than any retirement date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Can the gutter repair safely wait?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Hana and I would call a roofer to make sure the gutter can safely wait. We would tell our adult children about the postponed repair, not ask them for a monthly payment. A counter job would need enough pay, not just a friendly manager.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would the merchant job last?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The builders' merchant may have a posted opening, but robots could reach handling work around 2031. I would treat it as a paid bridge, not a lifetime guarantee. If the shop says it is only taking names, I would keep current paid files while offered and look again next week.

say: I would seek **written notice** and real paid work.
I would put the **mortgage payment** before a safe repair delay.
think: My **junior desk post** may end in the first year after 2028.
Our **sub-month savings** cannot cover lost wages.
do: Postpone the **one-time gutter repair** only after checking safety.
Check **posted merchant openings** weekly while paid accounts work lasts.
After **2028 loss**, take funded work with written bills pay, signed start and rota; otherwise claim eligible help and offered hours.
feel: I feel **alarmed** about expected job loss.
S2.quote: A nearly empty reserve makes the next mortgage date louder than any retirement date.
fieldNote: **Thinking AI** reaches his tax desk and merchant orders in 2028; only physical handling might bridge to robots around 2031.
The **gutter delay** depends on a safety check; a merchant move needs funded posting, written bill-covering pay, signed start and confirmed rota.

steps.text: Postpone one-time gutter repair only after roofer confirms safe delay
Check posted funded merchant vacancies weekly; move after loss with written bills pay, signed start, rota
Claim eligible income help and take offered paid firm work if no funded post

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years could let me ask the merchant whether it has paid counter work before my tax desk changes in 2031. Robots around 2034 could later handle stock, so I would not call the shop a permanent refuge.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the firm to post actual paid vacancies and tell staff the dates. I'd tell my family we need a wage through the change, not a retirement party.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I may be sixty-three when AGI arrives, but I do not know what pension will be payable then. Our current savings would not cover even a month, and the adult children have their own homes. I would keep working if the statement does not cover our bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This winter I'd request my pension statement and check the date and amount against our mortgage and bills. I'd keep the paid accounts rota while the firm offers it and look at posted merchant jobs every month. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2031, if tax work ends and pension income is not enough or not payable, I'd take only a funded counter post with written bill-covering pay, a signed start and hours fitting Hana's confirmed rota; if none fits, I'd claim eligible support and take any paid firm hours still offered.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about current cash, though five years gives me time to check the facts. A pension date is useful only beside the amount.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the pension statement change?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would bring the statement to the kitchen table and read it with Hana. If it shows enough income at a real payment date, that is a separate decision for us later. Until then the shop and the accounting firm must pay for the hours I work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would a familiar manager offer real work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The merchant manager knows me from client visits, but I would ask for a posted role and a wage in writing. I would not leave the firm because he says he may need help next year. A signed start would have to fit Hana's actual opening times.

say: I would require **posted paid jobs** and dates.
I would refuse a **retirement party** in place of wages.
think: A **pension statement** must show a payable amount and real payment date.
Our **thin reserve** still requires paid work now.
do: Check **pension amount and date** this winter.
Keep **offered paid accounts** and check merchant postings monthly.
Seek **funded work** after 2031 loss if pension insufficient; without a job, claim eligible help and take offered hours.
feel: I feel **anxious** about cash despite preparation time.
S3.quote: A pension date is useful only beside the amount.
fieldNote: His **age in 2031** does not establish pension eligibility or adequate income; the statement decides whether stopping is even an option.
A **counter vacancy** requires a posted funded role, written bill-covering pay, signed start and household rota; eligible support bridges failure.

steps.text: Request pension statement and compare payable amount with mortgage and bills
Check posted merchant jobs monthly while keeping offered paid accounts
Take posted funded role after loss if pension inadequate, with written mortgage-and-bills pay, signed start, rota
Claim eligible support and take offered hours after 2031 loss if pension inadequate and no post

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten years would put me at sixty-eight, but I cannot call that retirement until we know the money. AGI in 2036 still takes the accounting desk before robots arrive around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the partners to keep paying people while they prepare for another role. I'd say a free-market firm should state the wage and let people choose rather than offer vague comfort.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The mortgage may be smaller by then, but I cannot count on it being gone. Our present savings are under a month, and Hana's shop earnings vary. Our grown children should build their households rather than fund ours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd check our pension statements and mortgage balance each January while keeping the paid return rota if it remains. I'd ask the merchant for posted counter work only when there is a funded wage and a real start. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2036, if my tax job ends and pension income is not payable or cannot cover bills, I'd take a posted funded job only with written bill-covering pay, signed start and hours fitting Hana's confirmed rota; if none fits, I'd claim eligible help and take only paid firm hours still offered.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about the thin reserve we have today. Ten years of calendar space does not buy ten years of groceries.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would grown children help with bills?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Hana and I can review the statements without asking our son or daughter to pay. If the pension amount actually covers our bills in 2036, we can decide whether to stop then. If not, I need a wage and a start date on paper.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you open your own merchant shop?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would not put money into a new counter business while we have less than a month saved. A paid employer role is different from buying stock and hoping it sells. The firm can keep me on paid files while it has them, but I will not assume those files last forever.

I would keep **family finances** with Hana and me.
think: Our **current thin reserve** leaves the mortgage exposed when Hana’s shop is quiet.
A **retirement age** cannot prove payable income.
do: Check **pension and mortgage figures** each January.
Keep **paid return files** only while offered.
Seek **funded work** after 2036 loss if pension insufficient; without a job, claim eligible help and take offered hours.
feel: I feel **anxious** about current thin cash.
S4.quote: Ten years of calendar space does not buy ten years of groceries.
fieldNote: At **sixty-eight in 2036**, he still requires verified pension income rather than assuming retirement funding.
His **merchant alternative** is a paid posted role, never an inventory purchase; eligible help and offered firm hours bridge failure.

steps.text: Check payable pension amount and mortgage balance each January
Keep only offered paid return files while planning
Take posted funded role after loss if pension inadequate, with written mortgage-and-bills pay, signed start, rota
Claim eligible help and take offered hours after 2036 loss if pension inadequate and no post

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because the junior tax work could end before we save a mortgage month. I cannot say a pension will cover us at fifty-eight without seeing its amount and date. Written notice, a real funded local job and time to check our statements would help. Our mortgage needs a wage, not a retirement party.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask what happens to the roofer who cannot remember which job bought the materials. I can help trace that invoice, but my firm has to pay me for the time. A fast return with a wrong job code is not good work.

headlineQuote: Our mortgage needs a wage, not a retirement party.
portrait: At **fifty-eight**, Yusuf is a junior accountant drafting roofers’ accounts and returns.
His **accounting bachelor’s** accompanies below-average skill and senior sign-off.
He uses **AI occasionally** after testing and wants paid examples before changing the invoice process.
Hana’s **variable alterations income**, grown children, mortgage and sub-month savings make cash tight.
Low **junior pay** and few nearby firms make funded posted work important.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could end his junior desk wage before a mortgage month is saved.
whatWouldHelp: He wants **written notice**, a funded local job and verified pension terms.
